name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
causal_agent: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV), genus Begomovirus, family Geminiviridae
symptoms: foliage: Severe stunting Reduction of leaf size Upward cupping/curling of leaves Chlorosis on leaves and flowers fruit: Reduced fruit production Distorted fruit overall_impact: Yield losses of 90–100% possible in severe outbreaks
management: cultural: Plant TYLCV-resistant or tolerant tomato varieties Rotate crops to non-hosts to reduce inoculum Eliminate or control weed hosts Use greenhouse production to reduce vector access chemical: Apply insecticides targeting Bemisia tabaci, rotating or mixing active ingredients to prevent resistance Timing of applications is critical due to rapid virus transmission by whiteflies genetic: Breeding or transgenic approaches to produce TYLCV-resistant tomato lines
sources: Czosnek, H. & Laterrot, H. 1997. Tomato yellow leaf curl virus, an emerging virus complex causing epidemics worldwide. Adv Virus Res 47: 85–138.
Polston, J.E. & Lapidot, M. 2007. Management of Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus: A review. Plant Dis 91: 125–134.
Brown, J.K., 2015. The Bemisia tabaci species complex and TYLCV transmission. Virus Res 202: 150–162.
